hypothesis: Repairing the compact scalar-tail certificate restores validation of the inherited mixed integer/double/float, i64-only, nested and new retained-recurrence output interfaces. The output-interface boolean must survive per-reduction SSA tracing, and the bounded unit increment must accept both demonstrated add nuw and add nuw nsw spellings. This task preserves the inherited production legality extension: Bounded single-diamond compact add/fadd reductions can be extracted while arbitrary supported scalar state remains in the original producer. The inherited direct-use closure proof already isolates each moved accumulator from predicates, addresses, contributions and retained state. Removing the blanket ParticipationArm && RetainedState veto therefore admits state-dependent participating streams without requiring original-loop vectorizability, pressure/depth/reduction-count heuristics, a profitability model, benchmark identities or source rewrites.
semantics: Only the unused retained-state bit and blanket veto are removed in production; the existing recognizer, common participation arm, full-trip finite storage bound, byte/index ceilings, effect/load/call whitelist, strictfp/constrained-FP rejection, live-out rules and emitter remain. Each moved conditional PHI has exactly its update and bypass-merge uses; the update has only the merge use; the merge feeds its own backedge and final Exit LCSSA PHIs. Thus no first edge from extracted state can reach producer state, a predicate, address, contribution or another accumulator. Retained PHIs, starts, backedges, latch merges, operations, flags, branches and execution order stay on the original producer paths. Updates on skipped iterations remain updates; conditional state updates remain conditional. Every participating iteration stores its contributions at old P then increments P once, while bypass iterations retain P. With 0 <= P <= completed <= N <= M, all scratch indices are below finite full-trip capacity. The consumer reads 0..P-1 in original participation order and clones each reduction's operand order/flags; an empty stream returns its exact start without an addition. Ordinary unconstrained ordered FP and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering are checked in separate matrices; neither strictfp nor constrained FP is admitted and no fast-math/errno assumptions are added. Execution verification is requested for the exact unchanged historical recurrence_compact plus nine analogous integer/double-state fixtures: original IR, actual transformed scalar consumers and vector consumers/scalar tails, and independent C formulas. Retained fsub and fadd state, state-driven predicates/addresses/contributions, every-iteration updates, conditional latch merges, reversed PHIs, canonical +1, bounded +3 relational and masked-origin +2 controls, and enclosing-loop reuse are covered. New certificates reuse the existing retained-instruction, compact-count and scalar-tail/result proofs; typed producer/consumer scratch provenance, integer stream sharing and scalar FP operand linkage are also checked. Original-loop Selected/Rejected source locations and independent producer/consumer VF remarks are required before host specialization/instrumentation. Probes are inserted only after checking actual opt output; uninstrumented target IR is separately machine-verified by the harness. This repair changes no production LLVM code, emitter, semantic contract, corpus input or C reference. check_compact_scalar_results now uses recurrence_value for the per-reduction SSA value and leaves recurrence as the explicit interface-mode boolean through final PHI/store validation. The tail increment matcher still requires nuw, i64, the exact unit value and checked induction PHI/backedge/resume; only an optional nsw after nuw is added. All existing bound, predecessor, forwarding, ordered operand, typed reduction, result-PHI and observable-store obligations remain. Positive checker regressions exercise both flag spellings in actual generated inherited triangle/diamond/i64/nested outputs, six new recurrence vector/tail outputs and the historical delay output, plus retained LV1/LV2 four-stream float outputs. New mutations require assertion rejection for steps 0/2/-1, wrong induction inputs/backedges, original-N/vector-rounded/constant bounds, missing nuw or a different flag order, and changed FP output starts/values/types/store sources/pointers. The new recurrence mutations check the relevant certificate diagnostic; every inherited negative mutation is retained.
costs: Production adds no allocation, traffic, recomputation, reread, duplication, runtime guard, traversal or scheduling machinery. Entry scratch reserves M times each insertion-ordered unique contribution stream, with ABI alignment before each stream and no final-stream padding, still capped at 65536 bytes and the signed pointer-index limit. For i32[65] then double[65], reserved bytes are 260+4+520=784; reversed double[65] then i32[65] reserves 520+260=780. Integer-first M=1/255/5461 reserves 4+4+8=16 / 1020+4+2040=3064 / 21844+4+43688=65536 bytes. Two integer accumulators share the one i32 stream. Logical stores are 12*P bytes, logical reads 12*P bytes, total 24*P, independent of full-trip M and N. Scratch is reserved in the entry block, including entry-bypass executions in the emitted IR. P=0 performs no scratch store/load or consumer update. Enclosing rows reuse the same entry allocations with 24*sum(row P) logical traffic; capacity does not grow with rows. The preserved historical i32-only fixture reserves 260 bytes and transfers 8*P bytes. No recurrence arrays, mask arrays, chunk buffers or unbounded storage are added. Original input loads and helper calls execute once at their original sites/paths, including the original state-dependent rereads of input arrays; fission introduces zero additional input rereads, contribution recomputation or producer duplication. Existing entry and P=0 guards and normal LV minimum/vector/tail checks remain; no new alias/SCEV/FP guards. Production analysis remains direct PHI/update/merge use scans plus the inherited scalar-type/effects/live-out and CFG-edge scans, linear in visited instructions/uses/edges apart from unchanged SCEV queries; one state bit and a rejection disappear. Validation extends the existing focused certificates and shared transformation matrix, adds one small historical-delay certificate and bounded independent C formula families; it is not a general IR parser/equivalence solver or a target cost model. Physical stack traffic, register pressure/spills, RVV execution and speedup are unmeasured. The t000045 repair adds no production cost or semantic analysis. Its implementation is a local SSA-variable rename and a single optional regex group. Two existing lit scripts gain bounded positive/mutation cases; one additional opt RUN produces the inherited LV2 scalar-tail interfaces. No general parser, equivalence solver, profitability model, allocation, traffic, recomputation, input reread, duplication or runtime guard is introduced.

Nine analogous positive functions use two shared integer accumulators plus an ordered double accumulator. They combine integer delay state with ordinary ordered FP fsub state; the reversed canonical sibling also retains reduction-shaped fadd state feeding its predicate and contributions. The merge/affine/enclosing/one/limit siblings update state through active/bypass latch PHIs; the other siblings update state every original iteration, including skipped iterations. Header PHI order does not determine legality.

The new focused checker regression checks actual scalar, LV2 reordered scalar-tail and LV1 strict EVL output, precise source/capacity/ABI-order byte/stage-VF remarks, all six core shapes and three scalar capacity boundaries. It also checks actual scalar/LV2 tail output for the exact historical function. New mutations reject changed state starts/backedges/operations/order/operand order, changed predicates/addresses, moved/duplicated work, scratch capacity/index/store errors, count increment/bypass errors, wrong P/N bounds and empty guards/starts, skipped zero additions and reassociation. Positive SSA renaming and removal of retained integer poison flags remain allowed. Existing focused checker obligations are preserved.

The extended executable matrix retains every inherited comparison. New compact core functions run scalar consumers plus actual scalable vector consumers with scalar tails specialized at vscales 1/2/4/8/32; capacities 1/255/5461 run scalar consumers. Each runs separate strict and FP-reordering-option policies and one/two LV invocations. EVL core outputs are checked and uninstrumented RVV machine-verified but not executed on the host.

The independent compact formula computes exact N, P, floor(P/VF) and P%VF separately per row, including alias writes between rows. Modes cover nonempty producers with P=0, all-active, integer-state sparse, FP-state sparse, first-only and last-only streams. N sweeps 0..66 and UINT64_MAX for capacity 65, and targeted 0/1/small/half/capacity-1/capacity/capacity+1/UINT64_MAX for boundaries. Rows cover 0/1/2/4/5/UINT64_MAX; runtime origins include signed extremes. Integer bits, non-NaN FP bits and signed zero, NaN classification, exact producer/latch/participant/vector/tail probe counts, input/output canaries, aliases and entry scratch reuse are required. Per compiled variant coverage requires zero trips, entered empty streams, active/sparse where possible, first/last-only, capacity, scalar tails and exact/mixed vector paths when VF fits. At VF128 > capacity65, scalar-only execution is expected.
